title: Measuring AGI: Interactive Reasoning Benchmarks for ARC-AGI-3 — Greg Kamradt, ARC Prize Foundation
talk_summary: Greg Kamradt presents ARC-AGI-3, an interactive reasoning benchmark where agents must explore novel games with no instructions, sparse rewards, and no language, scored against human baselines on skill-acquisition efficiency (actions/time).

takeaways.technique: Private held-out eval set with no internet access
takeaways.what_they_do: Public training games let developers and models learn the interface, but all reported scores come from a private eval set the model and developer have never seen, run with no internet access to prevent leakage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all performance reporting will happen on the private evaluation set... there's no internet access allowed. So no data is getting out about this.
takeaways.numbers: ~40 public training games; ~120 games targeted by Q1 2026

takeaways.technique: Efficiency as a first-class score, proxied by cost and action count
takeaways.what_they_do: They score skill-acquisition efficiency, not just success, and since energy/training-data denominators are unavailable for closed models they use cost and number of actions/turns as proxies.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use proxies and the proxy is the cost. But then with interactive evals like this, you get another proxy which is um action count

takeaways.technique: Drop heavyweight engines for a minimal custom runtime
takeaways.what_they_do: They started on Unity, found it overkill for 64x64 grid games, and wrote a lightweight Python engine instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we quickly found out that Unity was way overkill for what we needed to do... we're actually making a very lightweight Python engine ourselves

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents are dropped into environments with no instructions and must explore to infer goals and rules themselves, rather than being told 'you are in a racing game'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We're going to drop AI and humans into this world and they won't know what's going on until they start exploring.

takeaways.what_they_do: They recruit adversarial testers to try to break the benchmark before launch, and run a mini agent competition on a 5-game preview to make contact with reality early.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're looking for adversarial testers. We want to pressure test ARGI 3 as best as we can.
